content: Self-attention: each position forms a query, scores it against all keys with a dot product, softmaxes the scores, and mixes the values by those weights.
Scaled dot-product attention divides scores by sqrt(d_k) because unscaled dot products grow with dimension and saturate the softmax, killing gradients.
Attention is permutation-invariant without position information; order must be injected via positional encodings, RoPE, or biases.
Multi-head attention splits d_model into h heads of dimension d_model/h, each learning a different similarity metric, then concatenates and reprojects.
Causal masking adds negative infinity to the upper triangle of the score matrix so position t can only attend to positions <= t.
A missing or inverted causal mask lets the model peek at the future: train loss looks amazing, generation is garbage.
The modern transformer block is pre-norm: x = x + Attention(Norm(x)), then x = x + FFN(Norm(x)).
Pre-norm stabilizes deep stacks; post-norm (norm after the residual add) becomes unstable as layers grow.
Residual connections y = x + F(x) give gradients a direct identity path, which is why 100+ layer networks train at all.
Cross-attention takes queries from the decoder and keys/values from the encoder (or retrieved passages); no causal mask on the source side.
RoPE rotates each query/key 2D chunk by an angle proportional to its position, so attention scores depend on relative distance automatically.
RoPE is applied to queries and keys only, never to values; head dimension must be even.
Sinusoidal positional encodings use sin/cos waves at geometrically spaced frequencies; PE(pos+k) is a linear function of PE(pos).
ALiBi adds a fixed per-head linear penalty proportional to distance, which extrapolates to longer contexts better than unscaled RoPE.
T5-style relative position bias adds a learned per-distance-bucket term directly to attention scores.
FlashAttention never materializes the n x n score matrix: it tiles through SRAM with an online softmax, giving exact attention in O(n) memory.
The KV cache stores past keys and values so each generation step only computes one new query; memory cost is 2 * layers * heads * head_dim * seq_len * bytes.
LayerNorm normalizes across the feature dimension per token: y = gain * (x - mean)/sqrt(var + eps) + bias; it works with batch size 1.
RMSNorm drops mean-centering: y = gain * x / sqrt(mean(x^2) + eps); cheaper than LayerNorm and the modern default.
The transformer FFN holds roughly two-thirds of a block's parameters; attention moves information between positions, the FFN transforms within each position.
SwiGLU FFN: (Swish(xW1) * xW3)W2 with hidden size 8/3 * d_model; the gate gives multiplicative feature control and beats plain ReLU MLPs.
Tied embeddings share one matrix between input lookup and output projection, saving vocab*d parameters; standard for decoder LMs.
Mixture of Experts routes each token to 1-2 of many expert FFNs, scaling parameters without scaling FLOPs; without a load-balancing loss the router collapses.
Encoder-only models (bidirectional, masked-LM) suit understanding tasks; decoder-only (causal, next-token) suits generation; encoder-decoder suits conditioned seq2seq.
Attention maps are not explanations: a high weight means information flowed there, not that the model decided anything.
Softmax attention weights always sum to 1, so the model cannot output 'nothing' for irrelevant context; masking removes positions entirely.
Attention complexity is O(n^2 * d) time and O(n^2) memory for the score matrix without tiling.
Not every attention head is useful; pruning studies routinely find dead or redundant heads.
In fp16, use a large negative constant like -1e4 (not -inf) for masked attention scores to avoid NaN in some softmax implementations.
Teacher forcing trains on ground-truth prefixes for parallelism; the train/inference mismatch it creates is called exposure bias.
Temperature T scales softmax sharpness: T->0 is greedy, T=1 samples raw, T>1 flattens; 0.7 is a common default.
Top-p (nucleus) sampling keeps the smallest token set with cumulative probability >= p, adapting the candidate count to distribution sharpness.
Always report sampling settings alongside generation evals; greedy for determinism, fixed seeds for reproducibility.
BPE learns merges by repeatedly combining the most frequent adjacent pair, starting from 256 byte tokens; encoding applies merges greedily in learned order.
Byte-fallback BPE can represent any input with no UNK token, since every string decomposes to bytes.
WordPiece merges the pair that most increases data likelihood (not raw frequency) and encodes with longest-match; Unigram prunes by likelihood and segments with Viterbi search.
Never swap tokenizers on a trained model: token ids map to different strings and everything breaks silently.
Tokenizer fertility (tokens per word) measures compression; a bad tokenizer on your domain wastes context and compute.
Character-level tokenization needs no training and has no OOV, but sequences run ~4x longer than BPE for the same text.
EOS must appear in training targets or the model never learns when to stop generating.
PAD tokens must be masked out of the loss; training a model to predict padding teaches it to emit padding.
Vocab size trades embedding parameters (vocab*d) against sequence length; size it with the model, e.g. 8k for ~14M params, 32k+ for 7B class.
Round-trip property to assert: decode(encode(s)) == s; watch leading spaces, normalization, byte fallback, and literal special-token strings.
Pre-tokenization regex (how text splits before BPE) is part of tokenizer behavior; two BPE tokenizers with different pre-splitting disagree.
A tokenizer trained on English-heavy data explodes fertility on other languages; match tokenizer training data to the model's target distribution.
Word embeddings encode the distributional hypothesis: words in similar contexts get similar vectors; geometry reflects co-occurrence, not definitions.
Antonyms often sit near each other in embedding space because they share contexts; distributional similarity is not semantic equivalence.
Embedding lookup is O(1) per token; its cost is memory (vocab*d) and its gradients are sparse per batch, so rare tokens train slowly.
Vector analogies (king - man + woman ~= queen) show relations can be linear in embedding space; they measure the corpus as much as the model and encode its biases.
Cross-entropy loss for language modeling is L = -mean(log p(true token)) over non-pad tokens; it is the maximum-likelihood objective for next-token prediction.
Implement cross-entropy via log_softmax (log-sum-exp), never softmax-then-log; the naive form overflows.
Gradient descent: theta = theta - lr * grad; the learning rate dominates all other hyperparameters in effect.
Minibatch SGD trades exact gradients for speed; the noise helps escape sharp minima, and shuffling every epoch is mandatory.
Report LM batch size in tokens, not sequences, for comparability across setups.
Momentum keeps a velocity v = mu*v + grad with mu ~ 0.9, damping oscillation and amplifying steady directions ~10x.
Adam tracks per-parameter first moment m and second moment v, with bias correction m/(1-b1^t), v/(1-b2^t); defaults b1=0.9, b2=0.999, eps=1e-8.
Adam's per-parameter adaptivity is why it trains transformers where SGD struggles: attention and embedding gradients span orders of magnitude.
AdamW applies weight decay outside the adaptive denominator: theta -= lr*(update + wd*theta); plain Adam+L2 regularizes backwards.
Exclude biases, normalization gains (and often embeddings) from weight decay; typical wd is 0.01-0.1 for transformers.
Backprop is the chain rule evaluated once per parameter via the computation graph: one forward pass to record, one backward pass for all gradients.
Always zero_grad() before backward(); gradients accumulate into .grad and forgetting silently sums across batches.
Warmup ramps LR linearly from 0 over ~1-5% of steps; skipping it is the most common cause of divergence in the first few hundred steps.
Cosine decay (max LR to min over the run) is the modern default schedule; set its horizon to the actual planned step count.
If loss diverges right after warmup ends, the peak learning rate is too high; warmup only delays the explosion.
Global gradient-norm clipping rescales g to norm c when ||g|| > c (c ~ 1.0); chronic clipping means LR too high or data pathology.
In mixed precision, order is: unscale gradients, then clip, then step; wrong order clips scaled gradients.
Underfitting (high train loss): add capacity, training time, or LR; overfitting (train low, held-out high): add data or regularization. Diagnose before prescribing.
Train fits, validation steers decisions (early stopping, tuning), test judges once; every decision made on test leaks into the model.
Early stopping: keep the best-validation checkpoint, stop after patience stagnant evals, and restore the best weights; it is a free regularizer for small runs.
Dropout zeroes activations with prob p during training (survivors scaled by 1/(1-p)) and must be OFF at inference.
Label smoothing replaces one-hot targets with (1-eps) on true + eps/V elsewhere, curbing overconfidence and aiding calibration.
Mixed precision: fp32 master weights, fp16/bf16 compute; fp16 needs loss scaling, bf16 usually does not.
Gradient accumulation: effective batch = micro_batch * accum_steps; scale loss by 1/accum and schedule LR on optimizer steps.
Xavier init Var(W) = 2/(fan_in+fan_out) suits symmetric activations; He init Var(W) = 2/fan_in suits ReLU; never init to zero.
Residual-branch outputs often use scaled init (divided by sqrt(2*n_layers)) because skip-path variance accumulates with depth.
The log-sum-exp trick (subtract the max before exponentiating) makes softmax and cross-entropy numerically safe in any precision.
Chinchilla rule: compute-optimal training uses roughly 20 tokens per parameter; small models are therefore always data-starved relative to optimum.
A complete checkpoint holds weights, optimizer state, scheduler position, RNG states, step counters, and a config hash; weights alone are not resumption.
Keep-last-N checkpoints for crash recovery plus keep-best by validation for selection; verify a checkpoint loads before you need it.
Perplexity = exp(cross-entropy loss); PPL 125 means the model is as surprised per token as uniform choice among 125 options.
Never compare perplexity across tokenizers: different tokenizations give different per-token surprise mechanically.
Bits-per-byte (total NLL in bits divided by UTF-8 bytes) is the tokenizer-agnostic way to compare language models.
Low perplexity does not imply good generation; degenerate repetitive text can score great PPL.
Evaluate with fixed-prompt generation samples, not just numbers; samples reveal repetition and degeneracy that metrics hide.
Eval gates are hard thresholds (PPL below X, no NaN, sane samples) a checkpoint must pass before promotion; automate the bar.
Test contamination (benchmark text in training data) inflates scores; screen with n-gram overlap and canary strings, dedup eval from train.
Token accuracy (argmax equals true token) is crude but interpretable and correlates with perplexity.
Dataset curation pipeline: language ID, heuristic filters, quality classifier, domain balancing; clean data beats bigger models at fixed compute.
Duplicates waste capacity on memorization, distort the learned distribution, and inflate eval; dedup exactly (hash) and near (MinHash+LSH).
Dedup across train/val/test boundaries, not just within train; cross-split duplicates are silent eval killers.
Sequence packing concatenates documents with separators to fill the context window, reaching near-100% token utilization on short documents.
Dynamic padding pads to the longest sequence in the batch, not a global max; bucketing by length cuts waste further.
Keep separate attention masks (which positions are real) and loss masks (which positions train); conflating them is a classic bug.
Pad on the right for training, on the left for batched generation so the last real token aligns across the batch.
DataLoader discipline: tokenize once and cache, shuffle before batching, use worker processes with prefetch so the GPU never waits on data.
Text augmentation (paraphrase, back-translation, noise) teaches robustness and format, never new facts; cap the augmented fraction.
Aggressive quality filtering can erase dialects and minority voices; audit what the filters remove.
Huber loss is quadratic near zero and linear far away: MSE precision with MAE robustness; the sane default for noisy regression.
MSE assumes Gaussian noise, MAE Laplacian; normalize regression targets or gradient magnitudes become absurd.
Nesterov momentum computes the gradient at the lookahead point (theta - mu*v) instead of the current position.
Loss functions encode a noise model; pick the loss that matches your data, not the one that is fashionable.
CTC loss sums over all alignments of output to input with blank tokens, enabling training on unsegmented sequences like speech.
LEVI's brain learns in two stages: a runtime knowledge base (ingested courses, no training) and a genuinely trained tiny neural network (proof the loop works).
LEVI tiny-gpt-v2: 6 layers, 6 heads, 384 embd, vocab 8192, RoPE, RMSNorm, SwiGLU, tied embeddings, exactly 13,767,552 parameters.
tiny-gpt-v2 training: 5400 steps, batch 32, seq 128, cosine LR 3.0e-4 to 3.0e-5, 100 warmup steps, seed 1337; held-out perplexity 125.01.
LEVI corpus records have shape {text, kind, register}; identity records (one per register, count test-asserted) seed the brain with LEVI's voice.
LEVI's held-out carving (carve_heldout.py) is deterministic and seed-fixed (20260921), stratified by kind, so eval gates measure genuinely unseen material.
Every LEVI corpus build writes a manifest (generator, version, seed, timestamp, counts, record shape, sources); a corpus without one is an anecdote.
LEVI working tokenizer: train/tokenizer.json, byte-level BPE, vocab 8192; the v2 harness refuses loudly on tokenizer/model vocab mismatch.
LEVI honest-limits doctrine: the tiny brain is proof of learning, not a capable mind; it learns spelling, phrasing, and texture, not reasoning or facts.
levi-brain is an explicit-only provider (--provider levi-brain); the deterministic local planner stays default until the brain earns more.
Canon 2026-09-22: weight-training data comes from Echoverse-engine simulations (hypothesize -> simulate -> train); external knowledge feeds the retrieval side (playbooks, seeds).
Two Echoverse engine variants exist (LEVI engine, LWP engine); brain-training simulations should come from the correct engine variant for the corpus.
The v2 run died silently twice mid-run (steps 4500, 5000) and resumed from checkpoints; checkpoint discipline is survival, not hygiene.
At 5400 steps x batch 32 x seq 128, tiny-gpt-v2 saw ~22M tokens: far below the ~276M Chinchilla-optimal for 13.8M params, hence proof-of-learning framing.
In the agent loop the levi-brain provider answers in prose; it does not emit tool calls.
LEVI's corpus chunking targets ~512-token records; chunks must stay within the model's block size or they truncate silently.
If a LEVI training loss does not move, the corpus is broken: the tiny brain doubles as a smoke test for corpus quality.
Context window costs: attention compute O(n^2*d), KV-cache memory linear in n with a brutal constant; match trained length to data.
RoPE extrapolation past trained length degrades; check needle-in-haystack evals, not just the config's claimed window.
KV-cache quantization, paged attention, and sink-token eviction exist because cache memory often exceeds weight memory at long context.
Sampling hyperparameters are part of the eval: unreported temperature/top-p makes generation benchmarks meaningless.
Overparameterized networks have many good-enough minima; SGD noise finds flat ones that generalize.
Weight decay strength interacts with the LR schedule; retune them together, not separately.
Too much weight decay on a small model visibly underfits: the model forgets faster than it learns.
Time-series data must be split by time, not randomly; random splits let the future leak into training.
A test set reused across 50 experiments is a validation set with a fancy name; rotate evals or accept the optimism.
Regularizing an underfitting model makes it worse; high train loss calls for capacity, not constraints.
The loss landscape is non-convex with no global-optimality guarantees; what saves training is abundant good-enough minima.
Adam's eps is a hidden learning-rate cap when gradients are tiny; raising it to 1e-6 is common in fp16.
Fine-tuning sometimes wants lower Adam b2 because the long second-moment memory holds stale curvature after distribution shifts.
Attention dropout placement (after softmax weights) regularizes the mixing itself; keep rates modest or heads go diffuse.
Embedding tables are often excluded from weight decay because decay on rare-token rows adds noise without benefit.
Scheduled sampling (mixing model predictions into training prefixes) addresses exposure bias but is fiddly and rarely used now.
For retrieval embeddings, encoder models are cheaper per query than prompting a decoder; pick architecture by task economics.
Decoder-only models won by scaling simplicity (one objective), not because encoders are worse at understanding.
Identity records are tiny relative to the corpus; they flavor the voice, they do not teach persona.
Rebuilding a corpus (dedup, re-chunk) changes the seed story; rebuild manifests and re-carve held-out afterward.
A retrained tokenizer without a retrained model silently breaks every id mapping; the harness vocab-match guard exists because this mistake is catastrophic.
Never claim capabilities beyond what the artifacts show: train_log loss fell, eval held-out tracked, samples textured; hype is forbidden by the honest-limits doctrine.
Head dimension 64 with 6 heads gives d_model 384; RoPE requires the head dimension to be even.
Fused attention kernels prefer power-of-two head dimensions (64, 128); odd sizes waste the fast path.
With tied embeddings at vocab 8192 and d=384, the embedding table is about 3.1M parameters.
Softmax temperature at inference is a different knob from the sqrt(d_k) training-time scaling; do not conflate them.
Prefix-LM masking: the prompt region is fully visible bidirectionally, only the generated tail is causal.
Batch serving with different sequence lengths fragments the KV cache; paged or blocked allocators fix the waste.
Changing the prompt mid-generation invalidates the KV cache; sampling parameters do not.
Stochastic depth randomly drops whole residual branches during training, regularizing very deep nets as an ensemble of depths.
Gradient accumulation plus a naive per-document loss weighting needs care; accumulation composes fine with packing otherwise.
Document order within a pack is a weak signal; shuffle documents before packing.
Eval on packed data must use the same cross-document masking decision as training, or the numbers are not comparable.
Model-generated paraphrases can launder hallucinations into training data; verify augmentation samples.
For pre-training at scale, augmentation is mostly pointless: the web already contains the variation.
Keep raw data and filter decisions (provenance); you will re-tune filters and want to rebuild without re-crawling.
Over-dedup can remove legitimately repeated content like licenses; usually fine, occasionally load-bearing.
Dead ReLU neurons accumulate in FFNs; gated variants like SwiGLU suffer less from dead units.
